artefacts.title: Architecture Artifact Instance — T19 — Stakeholder map

items.title: an approval row records a decision but not the trade-offs, conditions, dissent and commitments around it
high-level programme, architecture, analysis and project work is decided between departments and needs their participation on the record
meetings become the decision forum over the four existing primitives, never a fifth unit and never a chat
each decision is arithmetic over typed positions and the linked approval's policy, not a summary written after the fact
close_item writes one approval_decision per qualifying seat with via='meeting' on every deciding item
an item whose required department is absent defers with reason inquorate and cannot be decided
a change of decision rule or participation is a new meeting_type version, never an edit of a pinned version
the owner decides one item live in the web room and one asynchronously over MCP, both recorded via='meeting'
a forum that produces no decision over a cycle is flagged and, on the owner's ruling, retired

artefacts.title: Architecture Artifact Instance — T19 — Drivers, goals and objectives

items.title: meeting_type is a tenant-scoped, versioned policy row: agenda_sources, required_participation, quorum, decision_rule (unanimous|majority|chair), evidence_minimum, decision_window, timebox and allowed_outcomes; a version is immutable once a meeting pins it
a meeting is a card owned by its chair under WIP limits and DoD, with one live instance per cadence slot (uq_meeting_live)
the agenda is an L0 query over agenda_sources plus explicit meetings.agenda_add actions; a deciding item names exactly one approval with its evidence
attendance covers job_binding and app_user seats (chair, member, presenter, observer, delegate) with department, invitation and response state; delegation only where the type allows

one live position per participant per item: stance (approve|approve_with_conditions|reject|abstain|request_evidence), rationale, conditions, optional commitment, surface and time; immutable once the item closes

close_item derives the outcome by arithmetic: meeting rule and quorum first, then the approval's policy; the stricter wins; observers never count; a conflict-excluded participant is excluded by P4; a tie defers
the closed outcome set is decision|commitment|action|information|deferred; commitments become project dependencies or cards and actions become cards
minutes are a governed_asset(kind='minutes') drafted from the typed rows and published behind the chair's gate; dissent is kept verbatim and every action becomes a card

a human, including the owner, holds an ordinary seat and participates live in the room or asynchronously over web, Telegram or MCP; the first decision across surfaces is recorded once and via records the surface
participant-hours derive from attendance and duration as the third D52 metering source; a meeting_type with no decision over a cycle is flagged for retirement
the /meetings console lists invitations and seats, the room with agenda, evidence, participants and live positions, the asynchronous queue, minutes and actions, and forum history and load
no chat, transcript store or AV product; no calendar dependency (ICS is a read of attendance); no LLM selects items, decides, infers a position or marks attendance; no second decision store

artefacts.title: Architecture Artifact Instance — T19 — Solution concept

items.title: Forum policy management: versioned meeting_type rows with agenda sources, required participation, quorum, decision rule, evidence minimum, window and allowed outcomes
Convening: a meeting card per cadence slot, with chair, type version, opening and decision window
Agenda derivation: the item set is an L0 query over the sources plus explicit agenda_add actions
Attendance and seats: job bindings and humans, departments, invitation and response state, delegation where allowed
Position capture: one live typed position per participant per item, live or asynchronous, immutable once the item closes
Decision arithmetic: per-seat approval_decision rows and the stricter of the meeting rule and the approval policy
Outcome disposition: commitments become dependencies or cards, actions become cards, deferral and information stay on the record
Minutes as a governed asset: drafted from rows, chaired publish gate, dissent kept verbatim
Human participation across surfaces: the web room, the asynchronous queue, Telegram and MCP, with one decision recorded once
Forum metering and retirement: participant-hours as a D52 source and the flag for a forum with no decision
Console destination and seams: /meetings with meetings.spec.ts, and the T9 governance_body and T10 cadence consumers

No asset publishes itself; a human review decision completes the gate
No authored asset widens a tool grant; it may request, never grant
The dependency order is refused at the draft attempt
The target publishes itself through its own publish action; T17 drafts, it does not write the target tables
The live ingestion of procedures and policies is T16's capability
Each kind has one owning table and one publication row
The authoring job cannot publish its own asset
A policy draft that waives its own gate is refused
A draft that references an unpublished asset is refused
A reviewed catalogue publishes through the target's own action with its decisions
The linked drafts are proven without claiming live ingestion

items.title: An incident is a card with one lifecycle: open → triaged → mitigated → resolved
A destructive write needs an approval, a recorded dry run and human dual control (§6.5)
The four verbs are the only cluster writes; the read family is read-first
A postmortem follows a mitigation; a systemic finding opens exactly one kata (§9.2)
An incident whose fix needed no write can record a no-action mitigation and resolve
The tenant's approval policy sets the quorum; a one-decision ops gate is refused
Every state has one timestamp and one card meta block
A single-decision or no-dry-run ops call is refused before the cluster
Restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip each read back
A systemic postmortem opens exactly one kata
A zero-write incident reaches resolved with a postmortem
A one-decision ops gate is refused; a compliant gate proceeds

items.title: commitments: S03 commits to one domain and schema foundation every later slice builds on: the aggregate tables and their forced row-level security, the migration chain that owns them, and the typed store surface that reads and writes them. Tenant isolation is rls_domain.rs::the_fourteen_domain_tables_isolate_runtime_owner_and_superuser. The Phase-G review records the compliance level against this contract; the rework's acceptance instrument is acceptance/programme/S03.toml, and the closure gate is decided by an approver other than its requester on the P0-only gate.

The six properties are: (a) replay fidelity — 1,000 cards/10 lists with zero deltas; (b) one winner — one 200 and one 412 with the current representation, version +1; (c) 1k load — p95 ≤ 120 ms at 20 rps, five pages ≤ 500 ms; (d) webhook shape — {event,data,prevData,user} with the register event and *Out payloads; (e) SSE — card.moved ≤ 200 ms live and on replay; (f) no second store — one comment, one board_membership, no card_membership, no attachment. Each property is carried by a named test or command in plan §7. The snapshot records no Phase-G review and no run of these properties; this rework supplies the seven A–D artefacts, this contract, the Phase-G review and the closure review, records the level non_conformant, and re-closes on the P0 checks of the acceptance instrument. items.title: commitments: S06 commits to the control plane — claims, runs, approvals, andon, comms and notifications — as one durable boundary: one conditional UPDATE per claim with a monotonic claim_fence, one idempotent job row per period in place of fr's timers, one approvals.decide path with required_decisions and decided_by_kind shared by web and Telegram, an andon_state singleton that pauses the poller and refuses runs, and one message plus N delivery rows with a bounded retry.

items.title: compliance: S06 is assessed clause by clause against the slice gate of `acceptance/programme/S06.toml` and plan §7. The properties are: (a) golden path — card → claim → run → gate → decide → cards.move(done) with run succeeded and one audit, invocation and event row each; (b) dual control — required_decisions=2, one approve stays pending, the same approver again is 409, a second closes; (c) retry — a killed run is reaped as failed/crashed and the next create is attempt=2; (d) andon — engaged gives 409 and a 60 s pending run, released resumes within one poll; (e) delivery retry — a stub 500 lands attempts=5, failed, one row; (f) no timers — the setInterval scan is empty and every cadence is a schedule row; (g) human vs agent — decided_by_kind differs for one human and one agent decision through approvals.decide. Each property is carried by a named test in plan §7. The snapshot records no Phase-G review and no run of these properties; this rework supplies the seven A–D artefacts, this contract, the Phase-G review and the evidence output, records the level non_conformant, and keeps the project active until the instrument runs.

items.title: commitments: T2 commits to one decision ladder for every gate the platform asks: the four rungs share a single stored and returned audit shape, every decision pins the policy, refinement and laya-config versions it read, and a threshold change is a tenant refinement rather than a code change. The laya rung is an inference the engine performs and verifies, not an answer its caller supplies; option sets are authored and versioned rows the answer must match; and a generated draft cannot transition a card. The delivery is the ladder family and its migrations, not a parallel decision store: later slices call ladder.evaluate rather than adding a second gate mechanism.
